Guided 9-step educational activities for middle school (1AC, 2AC, 3AC), using your smartphone\'s real sensors.
Please select an answer for every question.
Activity 1: Measure the acceleration of a smartphone
Hold the smartphone firmly or place it flat on a table. Never throw or drop it.
In a starting car or lift, we feel a push as speed changes over time. How can we measure this change in motion scientifically with a smartphone?
Measure the acceleration components (X, Y, Z) in m/s² and distinguish rest from accelerated motion.
Equipment: Smartphone flat on a horizontal table. Prerequisites: Speed, motion and Earth\'s gravity (g ≈ 9.8 m/s²).

1. Place the smartphone flat on the table (screen up).\n2. Tap “Launch real measurement” below and start recording.\n3. Observe values for 5 s at rest, then gently slide the phone to the right (X axis) and stop it.
At rest: ax ≈ 0 m/s², ay ≈ 0 m/s², az ≈ 9.8 m/s².\nDuring horizontal motion: positive then negative peak on ax(t).
At rest, the curve is constant. During movement, acceleration along X increases then changes sign when braking.
The accelerometer measures rate of change of velocity (in m/s²) as well as the vertical gravity component when g is included.
Acceleration characterises any change in velocity and is expressed in m/s² in the International System.
What is the SI unit of acceleration?
Acceleration is a change in speed (m/s) per second (s), i.e. metres per second squared (m/s²).
When the smartphone rests flat on a table, what is the approximate acceleration with g along the vertical Z axis?
The accelerometer with g measures the upward support reaction balancing Earth\'s gravity g ≈ 9.8 m/s².
Activity 2: Observe the magnetic field near a magnet
Keep strong magnets at least 5 cm away from the smartphone and never place them directly on the screen.
A compass aligns with Earth\'s magnetic field but deflects strongly near a magnet. How does magnetic field intensity vary with distance?
Measure magnetic field intensity B (in microteslas, µT) and observe how it changes as a small magnet is brought closer and moved away.
Equipment: Smartphone, small school magnet, plastic or wooden ruler.

1. Remove nearby metallic or magnetic objects.\n2. Launch the magnetometer experiment and note Earth\'s magnetic field (about 40–50 µT).\n3. Slowly bring the magnet from 30 cm to 8 cm and observe the graph.
Far from magnet: B ≈ 45 µT.\nAt 15 cm: B increases noticeably.\nAt 8 cm: B reaches several hundred µT.
As the distance between the magnet and the smartphone decreases, the magnetic field B (in µT) increases sharply.
A magnet creates a magnetic field around it whose intensity decreases rapidly with distance from its poles.
Magnetic field is measured in teslas (T) or microteslas (µT, 1 µT = 10⁻⁶ T). Its intensity increases near a magnet.
Which unit is commonly used by the smartphone magnetometer to express magnetic field?
Magnetic field is expressed in teslas (T) or microteslas (µT) for weak fields.
What happens to the measured magnetic field when the magnet is moved away from the sensor?
It decreases gradually towards Earth\'s magnetic field value
It stays infinite regardless of distance
It turns into a temperature in °C
A magnet\'s magnetic influence decreases rapidly with distance until only Earth\'s field remains.
Activity 3: Measure the frequency of a sound
Sensor: Microphone (Hz) • Levels: 2AC (Acoustics and sound waves)
Use a moderate sound volume. Never produce loud sounds close to your ears or directly against the microphone.
A guitar string or tuning fork produces a low or high pitch. Which physical quantity distinguishes a low sound from a high-pitched sound?
Measure the fundamental frequency f (in hertz, Hz) of a periodic sound using the microphone and relate pitch to frequency.
Equipment: Smartphone (microphone permission granted), tuning fork (e.g. A 440 Hz), recorder or whistle.

1. Launch the sound frequency measurement (Audio Autocorrelation).\n2. Strike the tuning fork or whistle a steady note 20 cm from the microphone.\n3. Read the frequency in Hz and period in ms, then repeat with a higher pitch.
Tuning fork: f ≈ 440 Hz.\nHigher whistle: frequency exceeds 800 Hz and period decreases.
A steady note shows a regular periodic waveform. The higher the pitch, the greater the frequency in Hz.
Frequency f is the number of vibrations per second (f = 1 / T) and determines the perceived pitch of the sound.
Sound frequency is expressed in hertz (Hz). A high-pitched sound has a higher frequency than a low-pitched sound.
In which unit is the frequency of a sound expressed?
Frequency is the number of cycles per second and is expressed in hertz (Hz).
Between two sounds of 250 Hz and 800 Hz, which one has the higher pitch?
The higher the frequency of a sound, the higher its pitch.

Scientific and educational app that turns an Android smartphone into an experimental physics laboratory. It is intended for middle school physics and chemistry students and teachers.

Physique Explicite Lab works offline for local experiments.

• Sensor measurements are processed on your device. The app has no user account, contains no advertising or analytics tool, and sends no data to the publisher or to third parties.

• The microphone is only used during a sound measurement. The camera is only used for camera experiments. Location (GPS) is only used for position and speed experiments. Bluetooth is only used to connect to external sensors that you choose. These permissions are requested when they are needed.

• Saved measurements, favourites and preferences are stored in the private space of the app. Automatic Android backup is disabled to protect this data.

• Network exchanges only happen if you trigger them: remote access to an experiment from a computer on the same network, network experiments, importing an experiment by address or QR code, opening an external link. Remote access is not encrypted: use it only on a trusted network.

• Data export and sharing only happen at your request, through the Android share menu.

You can delete your data at any time by uninstalling the app or clearing its storage in the Android settings.
